surfaces.part: reading desk with open book (slanted top)
pedestal shaft with two small gold studs and cross-bands

answer.evidence: The wide head (14 px, rows 4-12) is a book/reading surface. Cream pages with grey text lines run rows 4-11, about 8 rows, and a brown edge line at row 12 ends them. Rows 13-14 are darker shadow and wood underside, with a red bookmark, and below them the narrow pedestal (3 px wide, rows 15-26) and foot (rows 27-29) form the front face and supports. The top surface is much taller than a 1-2 row rim and ends in a front-edge line plus shadow, as in the green reference lectern. It is not a flat front panel like the red one.

styleAnswer.evidence: The lectern is a small, fairly thin prop. It has an open book with page lines on a wooden stem and base. The measured facts support it. It shows 11 visible tones per full tile, above prop-hedge at 9 and below the stall at 17 and the well at 20. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown rather than black and reads as a dark material tone. Its 14 distinct colours match the bench and lamp, which are also thin props. Shading is about 4 steps on the wood and 2-3 on the pages, against about 5 on the richer references, so it is a little shallower. It does not look like a flat sticker beside the references. Judged by eye against the bench and lamp, it holds up as an equal-quality small prop.

surfaces.part: reading desk with open book (sloped top)

answer.evidence: The reading desk spans rows 4-11. The silhouette widens from 8 to 12 to 14 px, and the cream page surface carries gray text stripes. At x=4 and x=11 it ends in a front-edge line at row 12 (#885a26), followed by dark eave shadow on rows 13-14 (#633712, with a red bookmark at x=8). Below it a 3 px pole (rows 15-26) and a wider foot (rows 27-29) form the front support, 18 rows in total (12-29). The top is read as a sloped reading surface with edge and eave, as in the green lectern reference, not as a bare front band.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small lectern: an open book with text lines on a brown pole stand with a flared base. It is thin and sparse like the lamp-crook and bench references. Measured facts support it: 11 visible tones per full tile (the hedge has 9, the cheese stall 17, the well 20), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted brown rather than a black sticker line. The book pages show cream tones with ink lines, and the wood has a highlight, mid and dark step. It has about 4 steps per material against 5-6 on the references, so it is a little simpler than the richer props. There are no flat fills of 5x5 or larger, and it would sit acceptably next to the bench and lamp without looking flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: reading slope with open pages (lectern top)
desk front face with red bookmark

answer.evidence: The wide top (14 px, rows 4-11) is the lectern's reading surface with the open book's pages on it. It is framed by wood at the left and right edges and ends in a lighter brown front-edge line at row 12 (#885a26). Dark eave shadow follows on rows 13-14, with the red bookmark hanging over it. Below, a narrow 3 px stem (rows 15-26) and a wider foot (rows 27-29) form the front face, which is about 18 rows. This matches the green lectern reference, where the book sits on a slab with a visible front edge and shadow. The top could be read as the book alone and so as decor, but the wooden frame and edge line make it the lectern's own top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The lectern is a small prop of about 14x22 source pixels, so it is comparable to the bench, lamp and hedge rather than the larger stall or well. Measured facts: 11 visible tones in its full tile, which is above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted, a dark brown next to the wood stand and book cover, not a black sticker line. By eye, the book has cream pages with text-line dots and a lit edge. The stand has a few wood steps (light, mid, dark) with a darker base. It has about 4 steps per material against the reference's 5-6 and only 14 colours in total, so it is slightly leaner than the richer references. It sits comfortably beside the hedge and lamp without looking thinner or more sticker-like, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.

answer.evidence: The top of the lectern is a wide sloped reading surface (the book pages) at rows 4-11. It widens from 8 to 12 to 14 px and shows page lines. Row 12 is a darker brown edge line with a red bookmark. Rows 13-14 are a darker shadow or tray front under it. Below that, a narrow pole (rows 15-26, 3 px wide) and a foot (rows 27-29) form the front support. The pages read as a tilted plane seen from above, not a flat front panel, so the main top is about 8 rows. The foot is a thin base with no obvious top, but it is small.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small lectern: an open book with page lines on a turned wooden stand. On the measured facts it is at or above the simpler references. It has 11 visible tones per full tile against 9 for the hedge, and the well (20) and stall (17) are larger, busier pieces. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The share of neutral dark edge pixels is 0%, so the outline is tinted. By eye it is a dark brown beside the wood and the book, not a uniform black sticker line. As a thin, small prop it looks about as rich as the bench and lamp references, and nothing in it reads as thinner or flatter than they do.
